note: These are adaptive coverage prompts, not a questionnaire to print. Use only relevant branches; optional topics can be deferred.

questions.prompt: What kind of game would you like to make, including any genres you want to combine?
What should playing this game feel like?
What will the player be doing most of the time?
How should the supporting genres change the main activity?
Walk me through how one play session should begin and end.
What should reset, remain with the player, or require safe banking when a run ends?
How should the player build and use their deck during a session?
What decisions should the home base add to the next play session?
How much direct control should the player have over attacks and positioning?
What should a unit be able to do during its turn?
What movement ability should feel best in the first prototype?
What pressure should make gathering or spending resources a meaningful choice?
What rule should the player learn and use to solve the first challenge?
Which player choices should meaningfully change the story or characters?
What should make the player feel vulnerable or tense?
Which planning decision should determine success in the first encounter?
What action should the player synchronize with the music?
How do you picture the camera showing the action?
What visual style and atmosphere should the game have?
Where do you want to play the first prototype?
What tools, existing work, budget limits, or other constraints should I preserve?
What should the first playable version demonstrate so you can judge the idea?
Which parts of other games would you most like to keep or avoid?
What role should sound or music play in the initial experience?

response_policy.note: The coordinator authors suggestions from the actual session. These topic prompts are not complete replies or a canned answer bank.
